Sesquĭ-ŭlixes (Sescŭlixes , Plin. H. N. praef. § 24), as the designation of a thoroughly deceitful man (qs. a Ulysses and a half),
I.name of a satire of Varro (cited very freq. by Nonius), Non. 28, 12; 31, 30; 45, 2; 48, 31 et saep.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
